summary: Del Norte County lookout first built by 1923; its cab moved to Bear Basin Butte in 1997 and is rented there, while only tower piers remain at the original site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and a 1939 Siskiyou history give 1923 for the first lookout. The NHLR says the CCC built a lookout in 1934 on Upper Coon Mountain; the Forest Service says the CCC built one in 1935 on French Hill at Camp Six; the NGS datasheet dates its wooden tower to 1939. These point to different structures or dates, and the story reports all four without choosing.

The record's 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the NGS datasheet's 'about 40 feet'. The register describes the later cabin on a 20-foot open tower. Neither gives the cab-floor height, so height_m is left out of facts.
The Forest Service gives 5,303 feet for Bear Basin Butte; the NHLR record gives 5,145 feet (1,568 m). The story reports both and does not choose between them.
The site is gone, but the cab still stands at Bear Basin Butte as a relocated, rentable lookout that has its own NHLR record (US 288, CA 21).

notes_for_editor: Build date and location are disputed across four sources (1923 Camp Six Mountain; 1934 Upper Coon Mountain per NHLR; 1935 French Hill per FS; 1939 per NGS). The NHLR and FS pages describe the relocated structure at Bear Basin Butte, not the original site. The Bear Basin Butte record (NHLR US 288, CA 21) should carry its own history: the NHLR says an earlier Bear Basin lookout was built in 1924 and burned in 1936 after a lightning strike; that record was not checked here. The name Camp Six may come from a CCC camp on French Hill Road; a search snippet suggested this but no page was read to confirm it, so it is not used. No source describes access to the piers today. The Bear Basin rental is bookable, but the access key is omitted here because it describes the relocated cab, not the Camp Six site.
